contradictionsOrNuances.kind: task-text imprecision, not a hard contradiction
contradictionsOrNuances.detail: The task's phrasing implies THIS package performed the extraction of declarative contracts into scripts/qc/openspec-workflow-contracts.mjs and the addition of job-scoped requiredWorkflowJobContracts. Live diff evidence shows that module (and the sibling scripts/qc/openspec-ci-contracts.mjs, which actually holds the requiredWorkflowJobContracts DATA) already existed on origin/main byte-for-byte before this package, added by the earlier, unrelated PR #1647 ('ci: add OpenSpec contract modules', da524f7f5). What PR #1678 actually contributes for 3.1 is wiring scripts/qc/validate-openspec-ci-quality.mjs to import and consume that pre-existing module instead of its own duplicated inline arrays (a 24-insertion/122-deletion diff). The end state is materially what the task describes; the causal story ('extract... into X') is not quite accurate.

contradictionsOrNuances.taskKey: add-customizer-pr-regression-gate#4.1@22 (and by extension the R1.remote acceptance line 'Exact-main production browser rerun')
contradictionsOrNuances.kind: reliability caveat, not a contradiction of the task's own claim
contradictionsOrNuances.detail: browser-1667-main-proof-20260915.json's verdict is MIXED, not a clean pass: two zero-retry runs of the identical exact-main build (b39b8291) disagreed on exactly the test this task added (customizer-record-sheet-rendering.spec.ts:322, 'Print writes one current sheet...'), 11/12 then 12/12. paper-size-flake-diagnosis-20260915.json root-caused this as a genuine test race (workbench remount lands 15-50ms after the tab-click Playwright's action already resolved on, so a same-tick selectOption can target the outgoing unit's stale Preview instance) -- classified TEST RACE, high confidence, with a 2-line test-only fix designed (add an `expectSheetType` settle after the tab click) and PROVEN in isolation (probe: 9/10 fail without the settle, 0/10 fail with it) but NOT YET APPLIED to the actual spec file. The SAME flake also surfaced independently during the unrelated ci-task54-negative-probe-20260915.json run (PR #1680), corroborating the diagnosis. This does not falsify task 4.1's claim (the test was authored and merged as described); it does mean the R1.remote acceptance criterion 'Exact-main production browser rerun' cannot yet be called an unqualified green until the settle fix lands.

The [x] therefore reflects 'coded and reviewer-approved' rather than 'shipped', a materially different status than every other checked box in this package except arguably the CI-wiring items.
